briefs.topic: Robotics industry waits for a ChatGPT moment
briefs.evidence: Reuters reports industry expectations of a breakthrough in embodied intelligence while noting broad practical capability may still be years away and current humanoids remain less efficient than human labor.
briefs.category_default: Wait for the next model or capability breakthrough before redesigning the workflow.
briefs.deleted_constraint: A project does not need to wait for one universally capable agent before useful orchestration can begin.
briefs.new_competition_axis: How well currently available capabilities are coordinated into completed work.
briefs.bridge: A robotics expo keeps unveiling spectacular specialists while an ordinary project deadline quietly walks past them; InkClawAgent acts as the stage manager who turns available specialists into a relay rather than claiming a new robotics breakthrough.
beats: A futuristic expo audience stares at a covered pedestal labelled THE NEXT BIG BREAKTHROUGH.
Around it, separate original robots demonstrate one isolated skill each while a project folder marked TODAY remains untouched.
InkClawAgent rolls in a simple relay board: SEARCH -> WRITE -> REVIEW -> REVISE, assigning today's available tools to stations.
The project leaves through the DELIVERY gate while the covered breakthrough pedestal is still counting down.
briefs.punchline: 奇点可以等，截止日期不会。
briefs.visual_medium: photorealistic technology documentary with light cinematic polish
risk_flags: Do not depict or copy Unitree robot designs, logos or trade dress.
Do not imply InkClawAgent controls physical robots or has robotics capabilities.
Do not claim superiority over Unitree; Reuters story is only the cultural/news bridge.

briefs.topic: BirdTok and Gen Z craving something real
briefs.evidence: The Guardian reports growing young interest in birding videos and birdsong-identification apps, describing it as a gentler connection to the outside world amid a noisy online environment.
briefs.category_default: More AI output, more feeds and more content are assumed to equal more value.
briefs.deleted_constraint: The answer to information overload does not have to be even more generated material.
briefs.new_competition_axis: Signal, calm and useful completion instead of output volume.
briefs.bridge: A chaotic digital aviary has dozens of artificial birds shouting notifications; one real bird call cuts through the noise, and InkClawAgent converts the useful signal into one completed brief instead of adding another bird to the chorus.
beats: A phone-sized aviary is packed with anonymous neon notification birds all shouting at once.
The user adds yet another AI bird; the chorus becomes louder but the blank deliverable stays blank.
A quiet real-world bird call arrives as one clean signal; InkClawAgent catches only the relevant note and routes it through research, writing and review.
The screen now shows one finished deliverable while the noisy aviary is muted in the background.
briefs.punchline: 不是再多一只鸟，是听见真正有用的那一声。
briefs.visual_medium: social-native realism blended with an original playful visual metaphor
risk_flags: Do not copy TikTok UI, logos, creator likenesses or specific BirdTok videos.
Do not present the Guardian's cultural observation as a universal causal fact.
Keep all people anonymous and all bird/notification graphics original.

briefs.topic: New vocabulary for intrusive digital friction such as popovers
briefs.evidence: A Guardian culture/technology piece highlights newly coined humorous terms for familiar digital irritants, including modal/popover layers that obscure the content a user came to see.
briefs.category_default: Every tool wants another tab, dialog, login and interface layer.
briefs.deleted_constraint: Useful work does not need the user to manually traverse every interface layer.
briefs.new_competition_axis: How much interface friction disappears between intent and result.
briefs.bridge: A dungeon door is not guarded by a monster but by an absurd stack of original floating dialogs; instead of building a prettier dialog, InkClawAgent turns the user's intent into a route around the whole stack.
beats: OLD: a user faces a corridor blocked by generic cookie, login, notification, upgrade and tutorial cards.
OLD: every card promises convenience but adds another click; the actual document is visible far behind them.
NEW: InkClawAgent draws a clean route from intent to researched/reviewed deliverable, bypassing the interface maze rather than adding a better pop-up.
Final frame contrasts MORE INTERFACE with LESS FRICTION.
briefs.punchline: 别做更漂亮的弹窗，先问为什么还要弹窗。
briefs.visual_medium: original internet-native graphic metaphor with polished product-ad composition
risk_flags: Use generic original UI cards only; do not reproduce proprietary interfaces.
Do not claim InkClawAgent literally bypasses authentication, permissions or required user controls.
Frame this as category-reframing satire, not a security/access capability claim.
